title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-01-08

ai_review.summary: Rare early‑60s soundboard capture with raw, fair‑quality audio that showcases a surprisingly tight set and standout early Dead blues work.
ai_review.review: This vintage soundboard from an Acid Test in the winter of ’66 offers a historic glimpse of the Grateful Dead before they were even a year together. Reviewers rave about Jerry Garcia’s straight‑ahead blues tone, the band’s surprising tightness, and memorable moments like “Caution”/“Death Don't Have No Mercy” and Pigpen’s spell‑binding interlude, while noting that the tape is raw and a bit noisy by modern standards.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews (≈85%) are 5‑star, praising the performance and historical value; only a few note poor audio quality, leading to a strong show rating offset by fair recording fidelity.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Vintage tape with noticeable hiss and occasional muddiness – described as raw/poor‑quality but still usable; captures the era’s ambience despite limited clarity.

standout_songs: Caution (Do Not Stop On The Way)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑acid‑test set that feels free‑form yet surprisingly tight for a band barely a year old; the blues‑heavy numbers flow into psychedelic interludes, giving listeners a vivid snapshot of the Dead’s formative stage.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry's straight‑ahead blues playing and “spitting fire” from his Guild guitar.
